newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says EU decision a "mistake".
newsitem.headline: Turkey says EU decision a "mistake".

text.p: Turkey on Tuesday said the European Commission decision not to invite Turkey for EU membership talks was a mistake.
"This decision is a mistake. It is not just and it is not objective," Foreign Minister Ismail Cem told private TV news channel NTV.
The commission on Tuesday did not include Turkey in its list of six countries it said should be invited for membership talks.
But it offered a consolation prize, calling for deeper links to be developed between NATO-member Turkey and the soon-to-be enlarged bloc.
Turkey already enjoys very close ties with the EU through a customs union trade agreement which came into effect in December 1995.
Cem, however, said Turkey would not give up on its aim to become a full member of the European Union.
Analysts say a feverish economy, disagreements with EU-member Greece over Cyprus and the Aegean and a poor human rights record make that an ambitious aim.
Turkey's deputy prime minister warned that if the European Union went ahead with planned membership talks with Cyprus, Turkey would have no choice but to unite with the northern half of the island.
"If the EU doesn't change its attitude, Turkey and the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus cannot avoid integration," Anatolian news agency quoted leftist Bulent Ecevit as saying.
The EU has promised to begin Cyprus membership talks next year.

Ankara says allowing Cyprus to join before a solution on the divided island would be a one-sided move that ignored the wishes of the Turkish north and reinforced the current divisions between Greek and Turkish Cypriots.
The Turkish state in the north, proclaimed in 1983, is recognised only by Ankara.
The island has been divided since 1974 when Turkey invaded the northern section in response to a coup backed by the military junta then ruling Greece.
Ecevit, a veteran leftist who returned to power last month in a left-right coalition, was prime minister in 1974 and gave the order to invade.
